I have resolved the issue by ensuring the query's base table alias is initialized via `self.query.get_initial_alias()` in [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-p1o3q3rw/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1409-L1412) in [compiler.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-p1o3q3rw/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py).

Previously, when calling `Model.objects.all().delete()`, `query.alias_map` was empty when `single_alias` was evaluated, causing `single_alias` to evaluate to `False` (`0 == 1`) and fall back to generating a `WHERE pk IN (SELECT ...)` subquery.
